meta.heading: One follow-up: command output in labelled blocks
meta.intro: Round 22 is one card, from your note on round 21. What you approved in round 21 is being built now and your answers are under Done. This card is a plan with pictures; nothing on it is built yet. Press one of the two buttons; a note is optional.

r22-code-blocks.title: Command output in blocks that label themselves
body: You asked for fixed-width to fill in the kind of equipment by itself, and maybe only on specific blocks. This is how I'd build it (first picture). Paste a few lines of command output into any notepad and they become a block: its columns line up, and its label is worked out from the prompt and the commands. Cisco, Juniper, Linux and Windows to start with.
bullets: The rest of the notepad stays in the ordinary font.
Click a label to change it or take it off. **Copy** on a block copies just that output.

The one trade-off (second picture): while you type in a notepad, a block is plain fixed-width text between two marker lines. It turns back into a labelled block when you click away, the way wiki pages and MOPs already read one way and edit another.
The same blocks in ticket notepads, pop-out windows, Notes, the wiki, MOPs and the **what I saw** lines of a MOP run.
